headline: Shane Wright Gets Much Needed Fresh Start With Kraken Trade To Predators
take:
The Hockey News reports that Shane Wright, the fourth-overall pick in 2022, has been traded from the Kraken to the Predators, framing it as a fresh start after he never lived up to that draft billing in Seattle.

So far this season, Wright has three goals and one assist in 16 games, playing 14.14 minutes a night. His own expected goals (the quality of his chances) come to 3.74, so he is 0.74 goals below what those chances would normally produce. That looks more like cold finishing than a collapse. The harder part is the team side: SEA took 47.3 percent of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on the ice, and his model projection is 0.91 expected goals per 60 minutes, which is modest. His team's share is only 0.57 points better with him, so he has been neutral, not a driver.

The landing spot is close to even on process. NSH sits at 46 percent of five-on-five expected goals, a touch above SEA's 45, and the Predators' goalies have saved 5.5 goals more than expected, which has been propping up the results. Wright gets a team that needs help, though his numbers say to expect steady, middle-of-the-lineup play, not a breakout.
